```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

We use the `savings` data from `faraway` throughout the linear-model block:
50 countries, 1960–1970 averages. Response `sr` is aggregate personal savings
as a percentage of disposable income.

```{r data}
library(faraway)
data(savings)
head(savings, 3)
dim(savings)
```

## Design matrix and normal equations

`model.matrix()` builds $X$ ($n \times p$, including the column of ones).
We solve the normal equations $X^\top X\beta = X^\top y$ directly.

```{r normal-equations}
fit <- lm(sr ~ pop15 + pop75 + dpi + ddpi, data = savings)
X <- model.matrix(fit)          # 50 x 5
y <- savings$sr
n <- nrow(X); p <- ncol(X)
XtX <- crossprod(X)             # X'X, cost O(n p^2)
Xty <- crossprod(X, y)          # X'y
beta_hat <- solve(XtX, Xty)     # solves the system; never use solve(XtX) %*% Xty
cbind(normal_eq = drop(beta_hat), lm = coef(fit))
```

## The hat matrix

$H = X(X^\top X)^{-1}X^\top$ maps $y$ to the fitted values: $\hat y = Hy$.

```{r hat-matrix}
H <- X %*% solve(XtX, t(X))
max(abs(H - t(H)))              # symmetric
max(abs(H %*% H - H))           # idempotent
sum(diag(H))                    # trace = p = 5
max(abs(H %*% y - fitted(fit))) # fitted values are H y
e <- resid(fit)
max(abs(crossprod(X, e)))       # residuals orthogonal to every column of X
sum(e)                          # so they sum to zero (intercept column)
```

## Computation with the QR decomposition

`lm()` never forms $X^\top X$. It factorizes $X = QR$ and solves $R\beta = Q^\top y$
by back-substitution. The condition number of $X^\top X$ is the square of that of $X$.

```{r qr}
qrX <- qr(X)
R <- qr.R(qrX); Q <- qr.Q(qrX)
beta_qr <- backsolve(R, crossprod(Q, y))
drop(beta_qr)
kappa(X, exact = TRUE)^2
kappa(XtX, exact = TRUE)
```

## Rank deficiency

If one column is a linear combination of others, $X^\top X$ is singular and
$\beta$ is not identifiable. The fitted values are still unique.

```{r rank-deficient}
savings$pop_rest <- 100 - savings$pop15 - savings$pop75   # % aged 15--75
fit_bad <- lm(sr ~ pop15 + pop75 + pop_rest + dpi + ddpi, data = savings)
coef(fit_bad)                                  # one coefficient is NA
max(abs(fitted(fit_bad) - fitted(fit)))         # same fitted values
```
